name: Code quality

subjectOf.text: Increasing the number of reviewers who ask clarifying questions makes code simpler and clearer and thereby typically increases code quality, but hierarchical review processes make this impossible.
subjectOf.abstract: Moreover, the more people review the code with comments that ask for clarification, the more likely it becomes that the code becomes simpler and clearer, which in turn typically increases code quality. However, that is no possible in hierarchical review processes.
subjectOf.citation: Wulf A. Kaal, How DAOs Optimize Open-Source Code Reviews and Create Open-Source Standards (2021). SSRN: https://ssrn.com/abstract=3995709

subjectOf.text: The more hierarchical the code review process, the lower the quality of the reviewed code; hierarchy in review is inversely related to output quality.
subjectOf.abstract: The more hierarchical the code review process is, the lower is the quality of the reviewed code.
subjectOf.citation: Wulf A. Kaal, Code Review DAO (2024). SSRN: https://ssrn.com/abstract=4734750
scope_conditions: legacy code review firms with hierarchical reviewer structures

subjectOf.text: Multiple reviewers asking clarifying questions tends to make code simpler and clearer and therefore higher quality, but hierarchical review processes structurally block this mechanism.
subjectOf.abstract: the more people review the code with comments that ask for clarification, the more likely it becomes that the code becomes simpler and clearer, which in turn typically increases code quality. However, that is not possible in hierarchical review processes.
subjectOf.citation: Wulf A. Kaal, Code Review DAO (2024). SSRN: https://ssrn.com/abstract=4734750
scope_conditions: code review settings that permit many independent reviewers
